The scans#

This page covers both advisory scans Booster runs with plan, and how to run either one alone. Next: The dependency check.

The PHPCompatibility scan#

plan ends with an advisory scan: PHP_CodeSniffer runs the PHPCompatibility standard over the app and asks what will break on the PHP version the first PHP hop lands on. The findings are hints for the person doing the upgrade, never a gate: they do not change the exit code, and a scan that cannot run (missing tooling, a crash) is reported as "could not run" while the plan still prints in full. --no-scan skips both advisory scans.

The scan needs no change to the app: Booster ships PHP_CodeSniffer and the PHPCompatibility standard with its own dependencies, from the PHAR and from a clone alike. Booster looks for a PHP_CodeSniffer that carries the standard, trying the app's own vendor/bin/phpcs, then Booster's vendor/bin/phpcs, then phpcs on the PATH. When it runs Booster's own copy, it points PHP_CodeSniffer at the bundled standard with --runtime-set installed_paths, because the registration file that Composer's installer plugin writes cannot be trusted inside a PHAR unpacked into a temp directory. When none of the launchers has the standard, the scan reports a skip and the plan goes on; the skip says to reinstall Booster's dependencies (composer install in Booster's folder) or download the PHAR again.

The scan ignores vendor/, node_modules/ and storage/, because those hold third-party code and generated files, not the app's. It reads the app only and changes nothing. booster scan --path=../my-app --php=8.0 runs the same scan on its own, for any PHP version Booster knows, and exits 0 even when it finds a wall of removed functions.

The PHPStan scan#

plan ends with a second advisory scan: PHPStan runs over the app at the destination PHP version, using Pinstripe's base.neon preset. The findings are hints for the person doing the upgrade, never a gate: they do not change the exit code, and a scan that cannot run is reported with the fix that enables it, while the plan still prints in full. --no-scan skips it.

The scan needs no change to the app: Booster ships PHPStan and Pinstripe's preset with its own dependencies, from the PHAR and from a clone alike. Booster looks for a PHPStan binary, trying the app's own vendor/bin/phpstan, then Booster's vendor/bin/phpstan, then phpstan on the PATH, and for the preset it tries the app's vendor tree and Booster's. When either is missing, the report says to reinstall Booster's dependencies (composer install in Booster's folder) or download the PHAR again.

It ignores vendor/, node_modules/ and storage/, reads the app only and changes nothing. booster scan --path=../my-app --php=8.5 --phpstan runs the same scan on its own, for any PHP version Booster knows, and exits 0 even when it finds a wall of missing types.
